trickyParts: A kept copy carries the role topic in its envelope, so a consumer that delivered it would re-trigger role delivery on every listener. bus.DurableNotificationSubjects() keeps the kept prefix out of the one consumer filter built over the notification subjects (cmd/listener/durable.go); a test binds a real durable and fails if it is handed one.

Two numbers are needed from the cursor: the cursor message's own stream sequence, which the compare-and-swap write must name, and the kept sequence its body names, where the walk starts. readRoleKeepCursor returns both.

A forward that reached the server and drew no receipt (bus.ErrReceiptTimeout) counts as forwarded and the walk goes on, because that forward is stored on the holder's agent subject and a returning session replays it. T0 measured exactly that at both candidate bases before any code was written.

The drain reads the kept lane before the cursor, so a claim of a role nothing was ever kept for costs one stream read rather than two. Every claim write starts a drain, and a holder re-claims on its heartbeat, so that path is the common one.

envoy_role_kept_expired_total carries no role label: a role token names a tree role of one issue, so a deployment sees unboundedly many, and each would be a counter series kept for the process's life.
deviations: The kept answer is 202, not the 200 the plan's section 2 wrote. INFRA-514's architect decided it on 2026-10-31 after INFRA-771's implementer pointed out that with its T4 making every role forward stored-only, a 200 would no longer tell a sender anything was received. The three answers are now 200 (a live holder took it), 202 (kept) and 404 (nothing kept).

This branch is based on legion/INFRA-594 (sjawhar/legion#2446), not on main, by the architect's instruction of 2026-10-30: #2446 changes every file this change touches. The base was merged forward once at ddc0078d1e12, resolving two conflicts by keeping both sides (internal/bus/nats.go, packages/claude-envoy/tests/envoy-channel-stall.test.ts). The pull request's base is that branch; it is retargeted to main and main merged forward once #2446 merges.

Plan T6 added no fix to delivery.go's record guard: the double record was already gone at the base, as the plan's section 1 predicted, and nothing T0 measured found a path that still doubles. The rule is pinned by test instead.
The plan's T11 asked for the rig's two windows; a third was added, the keep:false control, so acceptance 3's listener half and both windows' negative control run on the same live stack.

The rig's capture subscriber had to skip notifications.envoy.kept.cursor.>: the drain cursor is listener bookkeeping rather than an envelope, and captured it failed the run's final envelope assertion.

They were run against a Postgres unpacked under $TMPDIR and reached through DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL, which is how CI's envoy-go job provides one.
